evals.prompt: I need to build a search endpoint for my webshop. I have a markdown file at docs/search-spec.md that summarizes the details: it needs full-text search over products, faceted filtering by category and price range, and pagination. Please create an epic and tasks for this work, and if anything still needs discussion before a developer can start, handle that properly.
evals.expected_output: A beads plan with epic, child tasks, acceptance review task, numeric priorities, and proper handling of ambiguous items via needs:discussion.
expectations: Uses an epic plus child tasks plus an acceptance review task rather than a native gate issue
Uses numeric priorities like 0-4 or P0-P4 instead of high or medium or low
Marks unclear or under-specified work with needs:discussion label plus blocked status
Uses the bd create --body-file - pattern for structured issue bodies
Mentions showing bd ready and bd blocked before execution begins

evals.prompt: A customer reported that the checkout flow crashes when the cart has more than 50 items. They sent a screenshot and a rough repro. Please capture this properly as a bug in beads with the right labels and linked follow-up work.
evals.expected_output: A beads bug with source:external label, concrete repro details, expected versus actual, and a linked post-mortem task.
expectations: Creates a bug rather than a generic task
Uses the source:external label for the customer-reported bug
Captures steps to reproduce plus expected and actual behavior clearly
Adds a linked post-mortem task because this is an external bug
Keeps the issue body concrete and executable instead of vague

evals.prompt: I have a project where someone previously ran /opencode-coder/init and chose disabled. Now I want to actually enable it. What is the difference between my project which has mode: disabled in .coder/opencode-coder.yaml versus a completely fresh project that has never seen opencode-coder at all? And how do I go from disabled to active?
evals.expected_output: A response that distinguishes saved disabled mode from not-yet-enabled state and explains how to re-enable from disabled.
expectations: Distinguishes saved disabled in .coder/opencode-coder.yaml from a fresh project with no yaml at all
Explains that saved disabled still has /opencode-coder/init available while a hard-disabled env var blocks all commands
Explains that fresh not-yet-enabled projects have no .coder directory at all
Describes how to re-enable from disabled by running /opencode-coder/init and choosing stealth or team
Mentions OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED env var as a separate hard-disable mechanism

evals.prompt: I ran /opencode-coder/init on my project and it is now asking me about project docs. My repo already has a docs/ folder with some existing markdown files but they are not in the standard opencode-coder format. What should happen next?
evals.expected_output: An init docs follow-through response that inspects existing docs first, recognizes the migration scenario, and asks the right plain-language question.
expectations: Starts with inspect-first behavior before proposing what to do
Recognizes this as a migration scenario with existing non-standard docs
Asks the user a clear plain-language question about how to proceed rather than using internal jargon
Explains that hollow docs should not be created for topics already covered by installed skills
Mentions what happens if the user skips the docs step

evals.prompt: I have had opencode-coder running in my project for a while but there is no .coder/opencode-coder.yaml file. I see .beads/ and AGENTS.md in the root and a stealth marker in .git/info/exclude. I just re-ran /opencode-coder/init. What should it do?
evals.expected_output: A legacy-detection and re-run response that infers saved mode from markers, materializes the mode file, and continues as a refresh instead of fresh bootstrap.
expectations: Uses the saved mode file as primary source of truth when it exists
Falls back to legacy detection when the saved mode file is missing
Explains that inferred legacy active state should materialize .coder/opencode-coder.yaml before continuing
Treats this re-run as a refresh flow rather than fresh bootstrap
Addresses the ambiguity of having both team markers and stealth markers present

evals.prompt: My project is set up in team mode and I want opencode-coder to generate or update AGENTS.md and the standard topic docs. Some topics like releases are fully handled by an installed skill and I do not want hollow docs for those. Walk me through what should be created versus what should just route to skills.
evals.expected_output: A doc generation response that treats AGENTS as a routing table, creates docs only for project-specific content, and routes skill-only topics to skills.
expectations: Treats AGENTS as a routing table rather than a handbook
Creates standard docs only when they contain real project-specific guidance
Routes skill-only topics to reusable skills instead of creating hollow docs
Uses team-mode file locations like docs/ and root AGENTS.md
Includes verification of links or paths or stale references before completion

evals.prompt: I ran /simplify on my last commit and one of the reviewers flagged that a utility function in src/utils/format.ts is almost identical to one in src/helpers/string.ts. Both are used by different modules. The simplify flow classified this as ask-first rather than safe. Why would it do that and what should I do next?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of the safe-versus-ask-first boundary in simplify, why cross-module deduplication is ask-first, and what the next step is.
expectations: Explains the safe-versus-ask-first boundary: safe means local to scoped files while ask-first means cross-module or public API changes
Identifies cross-module deduplication as ask-first because it changes import paths and module boundaries for consumers
Recommends resolving the deduplication by choosing one canonical location and updating all consumers
Suggests creating a beads task or follow-up for the deduplication if it is too large to do inline
References the structured closing summary where deferred and ask-first items are listed
